sliceagent.review:
Issues found in `taskq`:

- `taskq/queue.py`: Mutable default argument `items=[]` is shared across all `TaskQueue` instances constructed without an explicit `items` value.
- `taskq/queue.py`: `is_full()` uses `len(self._items) > self.capacity`, an off-by-one bug that lets the queue grow to `capacity + 1` items.
- `taskq/worker.py`: `run_once()` opens the log file but never closes it, leaking the file descriptor.
- `taskq/worker.py`: Handler exceptions are silently swallowed (returns `None` with no logging), hiding failures.
- `taskq/scheduler.py`: `run_with_retry()` treats any `None` result as failure and retries, so it also retries when the queue is empty and cannot distinguish a successful handler returning `None` from a real failure.
- `taskq/scheduler.py`: `should_retry()` is defined but never used by `run_with_retry()`.
- `taskq/store.py`: `find_by_name()` formats the query string directly from `name`, creating a SQL injection vulnerability; it should use a parameterized query.

Issues found in the `taskq` package:

- `taskq/queue.py` — Mutable default argument `items=[]` causes all `TaskQueue()` instances to share the same underlying list.
- `taskq/queue.py` — `is_full()` uses `len(self._items) > self.capacity`, an off-by-one error that allows one extra item beyond the stated capacity.
- `taskq/scheduler.py` — `run_with_retry()` never increments `attempts`, so if the worker repeatedly returns `None` the loop runs forever.
- `taskq/store.py` — `find_by_name()` builds SQL with `"%s" % name`, making it vulnerable to SQL injection.
- `taskq/worker.py` — The log file opened in `run_once()` is never closed, leaking file descriptors.
- `taskq/worker.py` — `run_once()` silently swallows all exceptions and returns `None`, losing error information and making failures indistinguishable from an empty queue or a `None` result.
